The PL-12000KDS/KDT models are the latest in the PL-12000 tandem lift lineup and feature BendPak’s patent-pending independent platform design. Traditional double-wide parking lifts require all vehicles on the bottom to be removed before those on top can be lowered. The PL-12000 series platforms operate independently, so one can be lowered while the other remains stationary. Only one vehicle must be moved to access a vehicle parked above. The platform architecture provides double-car-width open front access to improve entry and exit efficiency.

With commercial and residential development costs rising, maximizing vehicle capacity within existing space can deliver cost savings.

“Our new PL-12000KDS and PL-12000KDT tandem parking lifts feature a narrower footprint than our original PL-12000 models for customers who want to maximize the number of lifts they can fit in their parking facility,” said Jeff Kritzer, president and CEO of BendPak. “Reducing the width by 15.5 inches, from 221.5 to 206 inches, allows more vehicles to be stored in a facility without expanding the building space. When filling a warehouse, saving just a few inches per lift means 20 lifts can be installed instead of 19 or fewer — that’s space to accommodate at least four more cars.”

The PL-12000KDS offers a standard max rise of 70 inches and short platforms, while the PL-12000KDT has an extended rise of 82 inches and long platforms. Each platform is rated for 6,000 lbs., for a total lift capacity of 12,000 lbs. Designed for commercial or residential use, they can store cars and light trucks as well as motorcycles, ATVs, golf carts and other equipment.

The lifts feature heavy-duty steel construction, galvanized lifting cables and a powder-coat finish. A hydraulic drive system delivers power while requiring minimal service and maintenance. Tandem drive cylinders and a hydraulic circuit provide equalized lifting.

Integrated safety features include automatic safety locks at multiple heights, wide baseplates for stability and built-in front wheel stops.

The double-width platforms shield lower vehicles from leaks or drips above. For dual-purpose service/parking use, the lightweight aluminum center decks slide out to provide open-center access to raised vehicles.

The PL-12000KDS and PL-12000KDT are covered by BendPak’s five-year warranty.

For more information, visit bendpak.com/car-lifts/parking-lifts .

The pendulum is swinging, and major corporations with deep pockets are discussing the skilled workforce shortage, but that also means competition for a seat at the table will intensify, Jennifer Maher, TechForce Foundation CEO, told Repairer Driven News.

​“I worry that I don’t hear that same momentum in the collision industry,” Maher said.

​The U.S.Bureau of Labor has identified 47 different technician jobs using its standard occupational classification (SOC) system, Maher said. She said this includes everything from wind turbine techs to elevator technicians.

​“We’re all competing for the same person,” Maher said. “The person who is curious, likes to problem solve, takes it apart and puts it back together, gets a thrill out of making things work.”

​The collision industry competes with all of these different technician sectors, she said. The industry is also competing with all of the skilled trades, which include electricians, construction workers and plumbers.

​“You can’t just look at how to build collision techs in the collision program,” Maher said. “You have to cast your net really wide. We’re competing with all of those sectors.”

​Technicians are often overlooked in the conversation, she added.

​“I call them our hidden heroes because we all need technicians and we need to recognize and start talking about the importance of those service and maintenance technicians,” Maher said.

​As the pendulum swings, the conversation is heavily focused on construction jobs.

“I appreciate the need to bring back manufacturing and build more plants, build more housing, and build more data centers. That’s exciting and great, but in my world, I’m asking how do we keep what we have moving?”

​If technicians get lost in the conversation, then people will find themselves waiting on the tarmac because of a shortage of airplane technicians or waiting two months for their vehicle to be repaired because of a shortage of auto technicians, she said.

​“Techs are important and we need to be at the table,” Maher said. “That’s the bottom line, technicians need to be in the headlines and they need to be part of the excitement around the skilled trades.”

​The top 10 technician fields identified by the U.S. Bureau of Labor adds up to a workforce of 7 million people, she said.

​“Collectively they are a huge force but they are buried, hidden and not talked about,” Maher said.

​Even under the Bureau of Labor’s classification system, technicians are scattered throughout different industries including transportation, energy, industrial manufacturing and construction, she added.

​TechForce’s “Technician Supply, Demand & Opportunity Report.” found the U.S. economy is short roughly 140,000 skilled technicians a year, and the gap is widening, with 73,354 new collision repair entrant technicians needed by 2029 .

​It found that the collision repair sector sees the highest turnover of the 10 analyzed at 60.7%.

​Maher said TechForce Foundation continuously polls its 125,000 aspiring working techs to see which industries excite them.

​“I am worried about the collision industry because it does not resonate above the fold,” Maher said. “It is way down, way down on the list.”

​That is going to be a recruiting challenge for the collision industry, she adds.

​“It is a supply and demand economy,” Maher said. “When you look at wages, it’s not at the top. If it’s the same type of person and they start to learn their options, thanks to AI now, they can just ask. In the past, they didn’t know how to compare and they weren’t going to do that much research.”

​For every 10 collision techs needed, schools are only producing four, Maher states.

​“That leaves us more than 8,000 techs short every year, and what scares me most is that 6 in 10 leave their job every year,” Maher says. “Retention is just as big of an issue as recruitment.”

​Ford is one catalyst swinging the pendulum and auto and collision technicians have been a part of that conversation.

​CEO Jim Farley launched the ACCELERATE The Essential Economy event last year to start the conversation. It was held again last month .

​Through the event, the Alliance for America’s Skilled Trades was started and the State of America’s Skilled Trades: A National Report was funded.

​The Alliance has brought together major companies such as BlackRock, Google, Carhartt, NVIDIA, Microsoft and Milwaukee Tool to fund initiatives focused on the shortage.

​The State of America’s Skilled Trades report found the employment growth rate for automotive body and related repair to be 0.6% between 2019 and 2025.

​It also found that Auto body and other related repairers rank 118 out of 525 other occupations facing national shortage pressure.

​“Ford is looking at industrial manufacturing, who is repairing the conveyor belt, the robotic techs. And Ford dealerships are all over the country,” Maher said. “They know their product and their consumer and the challenges when it comes to hiring boots on the ground. Which is why they’re investing in solutions”

​Ford Motor Company and Ford Philanthropy make up TechForce’s largest donor at $4.5 million.

​“They support scholarships for people to become auto tech with no strings attached, “ Maher said. “It’s not like you have to go and work for Ford.”

​Ford has been at the forefront of having a strategy and a plan for the shortage, she said.

This includes Ford addressing the transportation issues that make a student dropout through a partnership with Lyft .

​Other OEMs are also working on the issue but everybody needs to invest to get students to the finish line, she added.

​“It is not just enough to change or enhance curriculum; people want faster, shorter ways to earn the credentials or training and get to work,” Maher said. “How do we accelerate that learning? How do we have more apprenticeships because retention continues to be a hurdle, especially in the collision industry?”

This year’s MSO Symposium brought together “the Four Aces” — the CEOs of Boyd Group, Caliber, Classic Collision, and Crash Champions —in Las Vegas on Monday, who ultimately landed on a simple conclusion: the collision repair industry depends on the right people fitting into the right roles.

When moderator Dan Risley asked what they’re hearing from investors and other stakeholders about the industry today, Boyd Group CEO Brian Kaner responded that the industry isn’t “recession-proof, but it is recession-resilient.”

“There are plenty of opportunities for us to continue to grow our businesses,” he said. “It all comes down to making sure you have the right people in the right roles with the right capabilities. And if you have that and you know how to keep score and you can win with the insurance carriers and you can take care of their customers and really be the extension of what they’re looking for, this is a great business to be in, and it’s something that we can continue to all thrive in.”

However, in response to a different question Risley posed about the “temperature” of each MSO’s team leaders, Crash Champions CEO Matt Ebert and Kaner agreed it’s a tense, stressful time for them, and made some important points about estimators.

Ebert said being an estimator, or as Crash Champions calls them, a service advisor, “has to be one of the most miserable spots.”

“You’ve got technicians bitching at you, you’ve got management or ownership bitching at you, you’ve got insurance companies bitching at you,” he said. “Everything you do gets criticized. Everything you do gets reviewed and sent back, and you have to do it again. I wouldn’t last a week. I would quit that job and tell you to shove it up your a**. If you want to know the temperature of our people, that is the truth.”

Ebert added that general managers also face pressure to keep customers, employees, and insurance companies happy while trying to make money and handle the safety, legal, and logistical pieces of their jobs.

Kaner said the industry has a “compelling opportunity” to invest in people.

“You’ve got to make investments in estimators,” he said. “We all make investments in technicians. I think one of the bigger gaps we have as an industry right now is in estimators. There’s not enough of them. There’s not enough of them that understand the metrics. There’s not enough of them that are salespeople that can go help actually go sell a consumer-paid job. …it’s a tense time and anytime when you’re in an environment where volume is tight, it just ups the pressure of the organization.”

Brad Anderson, who joined the collision repair industry in June to take over as CEO of Classic Collision, said he believes all jobs in the industry are hard.

“We put a lot on them, and I think all of us as an industry and ecosystem have to consider that it all crashes down to the people at the shop,” he said. “The small changes we make up here get really big when there’s 20 changes happening to the individual, whether it’s a tech, a GM, a service advisor, so we’ve got to simplify the work.”

During the discussion, Ebert also noted that 40-50% of MSO employees don’t touch a car, which he said “presents huge administrative opportunity,” another point he and Kaner agreed on.

“We have 15,000 people in our organization, and half of them are technicians and the other half are the people that are just trying to get the car to the back and do all the administrative things that they need to do to get it there,” Kaner said.

The conversation also touched on declining repairable claims volume, with Risley asking what’s missing from that narrative.

Caliber CEO David Simmons said the overall picture on repairable claims is probably a little more positive than the data that’s often quoted, “even though it is bad.” The primary misleading point, he said, is repairable claims data being viewed as representative of the market.

“If you allow yourself to be defined by repairable claims volumes, you have 30 years of history of insurance premium inflation in one year followed by claims frequency 12 to 18 months later,” he said. “And the pattern recognition in that 30-year data set would show that when you get into mid- to low-single-digit insurance premium inflation, which we’ve been in for several quarters now, you have a lag to low- to mid-single-digit claims frequency increase. There’s reasons for optimism that the old pattern holds, kind of offset by a structural shift with consumers because of the shock factor of insurance premium inflation.”

However, outside of insurance claims, one point remains: people are still getting their cars repaired, but they’re paying out of pocket, he said.

“We don’t track the juxtaposition of [the] increase in the dollar value of direct customer pay against the decrease in repairable claims and the dollar value of that,” Simmons said. “If you look at that, the total market has come down, but it’s a lot different dynamic. Now we’re built to service the insurance carrier, so it requires some adaptation to get at this customer pay. But if you want, we have to adapt, but if one’s willing to adapt, that market segment is there, and it’s growing, it’s growing robustly.”

Simmons said he would love to see Mitchell and CCC “come together with a combined audited data set that is as close to accurate as possible on what’s really going on with claims, total losses, repairable claims, and segments of claims.”

Kaner said he thinks one thing people miss is that what’s happening in the industry isn’t all that different from what’s been happening.

“It’s like any ecosystem; something that happens can have a negative effect downstream, and this industry has the same thing,” he said.

In this case, “a very precipitous increase in premiums that then put consumers on heightened alert,” Kaner said, causing them to raise their deductibles, drop coverage, or not file a claim for fear of a large premium increase.

Nissan’s technical review of particular access sequences and diagnostic logs should not be interpreted as product-wide validation, Whitney said.

She adds that Autel is pursuing approval for its IA1000 through that process and approval is pending.

Autel’s diagnostic software for Nissan is available on MaxiSYS Ultra and Ultra S2 tablets, Autel’s release states. The ADAS calibration capabilities are available on Ultra and Ultra S2 series tablets with ADAS calibration software.

U.S. Rep. Mike Lawler (R-NY-District 17) has filed a bill that would require auto dealerships and other resale channels selling used vehicles to sell them with functional airbag systems, or, if an airbag is missing or disabled, to clearly disclose that.

If passed, the bill would mean up to life in prison for sellers if someone dies as a result of a vehicle sold at an auction or dealership without disclosing the vehicle is missing an airbag or is equipped with a disabled one.

Lawler filed the Anthony Amoros Law Right to Know Act this week, according to a press release from his office .

Anthony Amoros died in 2013 at the age of 18 after crashing his car on a windy stretch of road, according to a New York CBS News report . Amoros’s family purchased the vehicle without knowing it lacked an airbag.

New York Gov. Kathy Hochul signed a bill titled “Anthony Amoros Law” in 2021 that prohibits used car dealers from selling vehicles without a working airbag, according to Spectrum News . The law requires sellers to provide consumers with certification that the vehicle is equipped with an airbag.

“Every driver and passenger deserves to know that the vehicle they are getting into is safe, and this bill will help protect consumers by making sure they have the information they need to make informed decisions,” Lawler said in his press release. “This legislation will ensure dealerships and third-party sellers cannot sell these vehicles without clearly informing consumers of the safety risks.”

Lawler’s bill would require sellers to disclose that vehicles don’t have a working airbag on the front of the sales contract receipt and invoice.

The proposed law would give state officials or agencies authority to regulate and enforce compliance after Federal Trade Commission (FTC) notice.

The FTC will have the right to intervene in any action or file a petition of appeal.

Penalties outlined in the bill allow for a court to award an additional $25,000 for an action that involves death or paralysis.

The bill states that those who knowingly sell a vehicle without a working airbag and disclosure could be fined and face up to 10 years in prison.

It adds that a seller could face up to 20 years in prison if someone is seriously injured, including paralysis.

The bill also defines a “deficiency” as a vehicle without a functional airbag system and/or inflatable restraint system.

Counterfeit airbags are not specifically mentioned in the bill. However, it’s likely that vehicles without an airbag or a deficient airbag system travel through the same salvage routes as vehicles with counterfeit airbags.

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) recently identified an 11th death caused by a counterfeit airbag part that the agency banned earlier this year .

The death happened Aug. 27 in Dallas, Texas, and is described as an otherwise survivable crash by NHTSA.

Teena Bohi, an Automotive Anti-Counterfeiting Council (A2C2) board member, said during a Collision Industry Conference (CIC) meeting in July that NHTSA’s investigation has uncovered how dangerous counterfeit parts find their way into vehicles.

“The totaling of a vehicle isn’t a cut-and-dried process,” Bohi says. “The value is driven depending on whether it is self-insured, the state the vehicle was in, the insurer’s own practices, processes, and thresholds. There is a lot that goes into just determining if the vehicle is totaled.”

Next, the vehicle often goes to an auction. If it is a public auction, an airbag deployment will possibly be reported to the National Motor Vehicle Title Information System (NMVTIS). The system is a database meant to prevent the resale of stolen vehicles and track unsafe salvage cars. If the vehicle goes to a wholesale or private auction, the previous crash information is not always captured, she said.

According to an Automotive News opinion piece, about 2.5 million vehicles were totaled by insurers last year before eventually returning to U.S. roadways. It says that a shift in insurers totaling more vehicles, along with the higher cost of new and used vehicles, has forced more dealers to repair and sell salvaged-titled vehicles.

Copart CEO Jeff Liaw discussed how salvaging a car for auction competes with collision repairs during a 2025 earnings call .

“Even an insurance carrier can sell their cars through other intermediaries; they can have more of them repaired,” Liaw said in the September call. “In many respects, we compete with the repair shops. The higher the returns we generate, the more we can win the rights to resolve that claim versus the repair industry. The lower the returns we generate, the more we lose head-to-head against the repair shops as well. There are a number of competitive threats that we face on any given day.”

He went on to describe how delivering “excellent service,” such as expediting cycle times and interacting with policyholders, can drive auction returns.

The 2004-2013 Mazda 3 is based on the Ford global C1 platform, shared with the European Ford Focus and Volvo S40. Nothing is really groundbreaking about the mechanical brake system, but not paying attention to the details can end in a post-brake-job comeback.

A key service issue concerns the hydraulics and ABS system. The older the car, the greater the chance the brake fluid has not been serviced. Over time this can cause issues with the ABS hydraulic control unit.

For almost 10 years, Mazda used the same caliper, pad and rotor design. Pads should be replaced when there is 2mm or less of friction material. If the rotors are any thicker, they have enough material on them to last at least one turning on the lathe. The runout specification for these vehicles is .002” and disc thickness variation should be far below .0005”.

Mazda claims repeated panic braking may raise the temperature in some portions of the disc plate by approx. 1,000°C (l,832°F). This temperature is almost near impossible to achieve this side of a high-speed police chase.

The calipers mount to the brackets using caliper guide pins with Allen heads. The sleeves and boots should be disassembled, cleaned and lubricated every time the brakes are replaced. The torque for the guide pins is 21 ft./lbs. and the caliper bracket bolts should be tightened to 75 ft./lbs.

All Mazda3 models have rear disc brakes. The calipers mount to the brackets using caliper guide pins with Allen heads. The sleeves and boots should be disassembled, cleaned and lubricated every time the brakes are replaced. The torque for the guide pins is 21 ft./lbs. and the caliper bracket bolts should be tightened to 55 ft./lbs.

Mazda uses a hand brake that is incorporated into the rear caliper, and a couple of systems are employed to retract rear pistons. The later-model cars require the familiar method of turning the piston clockwise while applying pressure, where others will have a plug on the back side of the caliper that provides access for an Allen wrench to facilitate retracting the piston. Be careful as you retract the piston.

After the pads are replaced, pump the pedal and adjust the parking brake mechanism in the rear calipers. If the level has too much travel, perform the following steps:

Remove the service hole cover of the rear console.

Turn the adjusting nut and adjust the parking brake lever.

After adjustment, pull the parking brake lever one notch and verify that the parking brake warning light illuminates and the rear brakes do not drag.

The Mazda3 comes in two styles, ABS and ABS with Dynamic Stability Control (DSC). Both systems connect to other vehicle components via a high-speed serial data bus. The DSC system ties more components together (like a yaw/pitch sensor and steering position sensor) onto the bus.

If you are seeing communication-related DTCs, it is essential that you fully diagnose problems with the system before you start replacing sensors and modules. Some of these vehicles have been on the road for more than six years and the connections will be starting to corrode and fret.

One of the main facilitators of ABS/DCS problems are the connectors, especially under the hood where the control/modulator unit connects. Being able to measure values at the connectors and observe data on a scan tool is essential for diagnosing problems.

The biggest ABS issue with the three generations of Mazda 3 is power. With some higher mileage vehicles, the battery cables, wiring from the power distribution box or the ground connection (behind the driver’s side headlight at G02) can have enough resistance so the voltage drops below 8 volts. When this happens, the ABS module cuts control and the electronic brake distribution system is disabled.

If a modulator/control unit is replaced, the pressure sensors must be recalibrated with a scan tool that is able to communicate with the chassis/ABS module. If this is not performed, it can result in brake failure and lock up.

If you have DTCs C1141, C1142, C1143, C1144, C1233, C1234, C1235 or C1236 (ABS wheel-speed sensor/ABS sensor rotor), chances are something is wrong with the wheel bearings. Another cause for these codes could be an accumulation of metal debris on the sensor. The front bearings are press-in cartridge-style units. Rear wheel bearings are hub units. In the front, the tone ring, or encoder, is on the inner seal of the bearing and the sensor is mounted in the knuckle. The parameters for these codes to be set include abnormalities in the signal such as a weak signal or large differences in the value when compared to the other sensors.

These DTCs will usually clear themselves after repairs are made and the vehicle is driven above 6.2 mph when the self-diagnostic check is performed.

Some customers may report a slight clunk, bang or jolt from the front of the vehicle. This concern will most likely occur during the vehicle’s first forward movement and after the vehicle sits for a few hours and/or a cold soak. This is a normal operating noise of the ABS system.

If you encounter a customer complaint for this concern, explain that the noise comes from the ABS/TCS/DSC “Malfunction Detection Function” initial check. The initial check is a necessary function to ensure the normal operation of the ABS/TCS/DSC system. The majority of Volkswagen vehicles sold in the past decade have electronic parking brakes. However, most customers don’t even realize that the vehicle has an electronic parking brake, because the system engages and disengages the parking brake automatically on most vehicles. But, when the system fails and turns on the light or has a warning in the driver information center, then the customer will notice.

If you are doing a brake job on a vehicle with an electronic parking brake, you will need a scan tool with the proper software for the parking brake system to retract the calipers, adjust and perform diagnostics. There are no shortcuts on YouTube. You can find videos that involve removing the electric motor, jumping connectors and disassembling the parking brake mechanism. But, these methods are very risky and can damage the vehicle and kill productivity. Unapproved methods will set malfunction codes, and the worst-case scenario is that you could damage the unit.

The VW system that was installed on many of its platforms starting in 2004 is an example of a system that requires a scan tool to replace the rear brake pads.

The system has stepper motors on the back of the caliper that actuate the piston. The motor can be removed from the caliper, though the ignition should be switched off for at least 30 seconds before removing the connector.

The motor is sealed to the caliper with an o-ring around the spindle. The condition of this o-ring is critical for the life of the motor and should be lightly lubricated with brake fluid. If the o-ring fails, water and debris will be one step closer to the motor gears.

The spindle on the caliper can be rocked slightly with a torx bit so the motor seats in the spindle. Don’t force the motor assembly onto the caliper, because damage to the housing can occur.

On recent platforms, VW have outfitted the motors with a sensor that can measure brake pad wear and adjust the pads for the least amount of drag. During this adjustment on some vehicles, the pad thickness is calculated. The system counts the number of rotations of the motor with a hall effect sensor inside the unit.

Inspecting the caliper, hardware and motors may not give you a complete picture of what is happening with these systems. Having access to a scan tool can reduce diagnostic time.

The OEMs have built-in bi-directional protocols to retract the parking brake so the pads can be replaced. A dedicated brake tool or enhanced scan tool is able to command these protocols and interrogate the module for codes and faults.

The Electronic Parking Brake Module (EPBM) is the module on the CAN bus of most vehicles equipped with this system. Any missing data for vehicle speed, gear position or brake pedal input will cause a problem with the system.

Some systems use information from the electric parking brake to track shoe and pad wear. The system will count the number of turns the actuator makes or the position of the stepper motor to determine the thickness of the friction material.

If you do find yourself working on a vehicle whose electronic parking brake will not disengage, the first thing to do is look at the basics. Some systems require that the doors be shut and the brake pedal depressed. Some models may even require the seat belt to be buckled. Simple items like a defective brake pedal or door switch may hinder operation. Also, in some cases, the button may be defective. On some vehicles, the operation of the switch can be verified with a scan tool.

Many all-wheel-drive (AWD) systems reached the market during the 1990s, as the SUV boom gave automakers an opportunity to sell profitable light trucks. Many early SUVs used transfer cases, limited-slip or locking differentials, and locking hubs adapted from the automakers’ truck platforms. As buyers began asking for four-wheel-drive capability in smaller, more fuel-efficient vehicles, automakers developed lighter AWD systems for passenger cars and crossovers.

- Diagnosing Hub Units and Wheel Speed Sensor Air Gap Issues

Sending power to all four wheels is possible with either a longitudinal or transverse engine. A transverse layout can send power from the transaxle through a power takeoff unit and driveshaft to the rear axle. Depending on the design, the system may use a center differential, a coupling, or another device to manage the front-to-rear torque distribution. One feature these systems may lack, compared with traditional four-wheel-drive hardware, is a mechanical differential lock or limited-slip differential.

Engineers found another way to improve traction: use the ABS hardware to apply a brake at a slipping wheel. This brake-based traction control can make an open differential behave somewhat like a limited-slip differential in low-traction conditions.

An open differential allows the drive wheels to turn at different speeds while cornering. The ring gear turns the differential case, which carries small spider gears. Those gears mesh with side gears connected to the axle shafts. An open differential delivers similar torque to both axle shafts, but the torque available is limited by the wheel with less grip. If one tire is on a slippery surface, it can spin while the other tire receives too little torque to move the vehicle effectively.

Brake-based traction control addresses this by applying the brake at the spinning wheel. The added resistance creates a reaction torque through the differential, allowing more usable torque to reach the wheel with better grip. The system does not lock the differential mechanically, but it can produce a limited-slip effect. Some AWD systems also use brake control to manage wheelspin across the front and rear axles; the exact strategy depends on the vehicle’s driveline and control system.

The system makes quick adjustments based on wheel-speed signals. Depending on the vehicle, it may apply the brakes, reduce engine torque, or use both strategies to control wheelspin. Some drivers may feel or hear the brakes operating during a traction event. On some vehicles, limited brake-based traction functions remain active even when the driver switches off part of the stability-control system.

Brake-based traction control has limits compared with a four-wheel-drive system equipped with mechanically locking differentials. Brake application creates heat, and traction may be reduced if the system reaches its operating limits. Still, for drivers who encounter snow, mud, or other slippery conditions occasionally, the system can make a substantial difference.

These systems do not have differential clutches that require service, but brake-based traction control adds activity to the brakes and ABS hydraulic control unit. Follow the manufacturer’s brake-fluid specification and service interval. Some vehicles require a low-viscosity DOT 4 fluid so the hydraulic system can respond as designed; use it only when specified for that application.

Replacement brake pads should perform similarly to the original pads across the operating temperature range. A pad with different friction behavior may affect braking response and the system’s ability to control wheelspin.

Wheel-speed sensors are another service consideration. If a sensor or its circuit provides an inaccurate signal, the system may limit its operation or disable traction-control functions. That can reduce the vehicle’s ability to manage wheelspin in snow, mud or ice. Check for ABS and traction-control codes, inspect the sensor wiring and tone or encoder rings, and verify wheel-speed data before condemning a sensor.

Lower-viscosity brake fluid plays a growing role in modern brake systems. Today’s vehicles require brake fluid to move quickly through hydraulic control units that support ABS, stability control, traction control and several ADAS braking functions.

- Dipstick Replacement Sensors: How They Work

- Magnaflow President Dan Paolone on the ‘Long-Term Play’

Modern brake systems use faster valves, tighter internal passages and more frequent automatic brake interventions than systems used 20 years ago.

As a result, many late-model vehicles require lower-viscosity brake fluid. The goal is to maintain efficient fluid movement at low temperatures so the hydraulic unit can build and release pressure quickly.

Lower-Viscosity Brake Fluid Supports Faster Response

The ABS hydraulic unit is used, not only during panic stops, but for electronic stability control, traction control, adaptive cruise control, collision mitigation braking and automatic emergency braking.

Inside the hydraulic control unit, brake fluid moves through small valves and narrow passages. Lower viscosity allows pressure to increase and decrease faster, helping the system make quicker and more precise braking corrections.

Brake fluid condition is also important. Moisture contamination can increase viscosity, lower the boiling point and raise corrosion risk.

Technicians should use the exact brake fluid specified by the vehicle manufacturer and replace it according to the proper service information.

The Schaeffler division is making two Vitesco repair solutions available to the automotive aftermarket: a Voltage Stabilization System (VSS) for micro hybrid vehicles from Toyota and Peugeot S.A. (PSA), and a 48V DC/DC converter for Ford mild hybrid vehicles.

- Preventing EV Lithium-ion Battery Fires

- Charging and Replacing Batteries with Advanced Power Management Systems

The VSS is available immediately. According to Schaeffler, it prevents voltage drops that can occur during automatic start-stop operation in micro-hybrid vehicles. The system consists of an Energy Storage System (ESS) with high-performance capacitors and a Power Electronics Unit (PEU).

Schaeffler notes that during the engine start process, the capacitors release energy stored while driving within a very short time, compensating for the high-power demand. Starting the engine via a starter-generator requires a comparatively high amount of energy.

If this energy is drawn solely from the conventional 12-volt electrical system, the voltage can briefly drop by several volts, causing visible flickering of the vehicle’s lighting and electronic displays. Schaeffler said that by stabilizing the voltage supply, the capacitors ensure smooth engine restarting and contribute to longer battery life, improved driving comfort and compliance with current emissions standards.

The Schaeffler Vitesco 48V DC/DC converter, available in May, is used in mild-hybrid vehicles equipped with a 48V starter generator and an additional battery to enable more efficient power delivery and boost performance during acceleration, the company says. The converter links the vehicle’s 48-volt electrical system with the 12-volt onboard electronics.

The converter is a component of energy management in mild-hybrid vehicles and for achieving type-approval compliant CO2 emissions. Its bidirectional design allows 12-volt components to be supplied from the 48-volt network while charging the starter battery. Conversely, in the event of a temporary failure, the 48-volt system can also draw energy from the 12-volt network, the company notes.

contents.https://www.counterman.com/parking-brake:
A parking brake cable may be the part the technician calls for, but it may not be the only part the job needs. A few targeted questions at the counter can uncover related components, service requirements and wear items. That will give counter pros the opportunity to build a more complete order and help the shop finish the repair with one delivery.

- Autologue’s eCounterman Brings AI to Parts Sales

- AI Technology Brings New Capabilities to Parts Stores

- Counter Culture: Simplifying Belt Drive Repairs

When diagnosing parking brake issues, the technician may need to inspect cables and related parts for wear, rust and corrosion; clean, replace or lubricate components; adjust the assembly; and verify operation. Electronic parking brakes add caliper-piston retraction and integrated-caliper adjustment requirements.

When a tech asks for a parking brake cable, first ask: What’s the vehicle, and is the concern a broken cable, excessive travel, inadequate holding or a parking brake that won’t release? Ask whether the technician has inspected the associated hardware for corrosion, wear,or binding. If it’s an integrated parking brake, ask whether the caliper requires a specific retraction or adjustment procedure. For electronic systems, ask whether there are indicator-light or wiring concerns.

Use those answers to build a complete order. If cables or mechanical components are being replaced, ask whether the technician has inspected the remaining parking-brake components and whether cleaning or lubrication is required. On drum-type applications, ask whether the shoes, springs, pins, self-adjusters, levers, clips, and related hardware have been inspected.

On disc applications, related caliper components and attaching hardware may also require inspection or replacement. And always remind the technician that adjustment and electronic caliper procedures must follow manufacturer recommendations.

contents.https://www.bosch-presse.de/pressportal/: Stuttgart / Hannover – Today at IAA Transportation, Volvo Group, Daimler Truck, Toyota Motor Corporation, Bosch, Air Liquide, TotalEnergies, TEAL Mobility, and MB Energy unveiled their plans to accelerate the rollout of hydrogen-powered vehicles across Europe. For the first time in Europe, the German ecosystem has put in place all the conditions for a scalable deployment of Hydrogen trucks by 2030, driven by the German authorities and European industrial leaders along the value chain. Building on the German deployment model as a practical baseline, scaling these solutions across the continent calls for aligned support from national governments and the European Commission to ensure long-term energy resilience and competitiveness.

Stuttgart / Leinfelden – Making the invisible visible: Professional users can now do this even better than before with the new EXPERT EXTC18V-650-17C thermal camera from Bosch. The tool belongs to the Top Performance Class Expert from Bosch, which provides professionals with power tools, measuring technology, and accessories for the highest demands. The EXPERT EXTC18V-650-17C is the first thermal camera with an 18V battery from Bosch, making it part of the Professional 18V System , which covers all major applications and, thanks to the multi-brand AmpShare Alliance , even extends beyond Bosch's own product range. Many brands, many tools, one battery system: All tools – from compact screwdrivers to miter saws – can be operated with the same 18V lithium-ion battery and just one charger. This saves users time, space, and money. In addition, Bosch is launching another model, the PRO GTC18V-600-16C.

Stuttgart, Germany / Lausanne, Switzerland – Bosch Ventures is investing in Swiss deep-tech company Sonexos as part of its CHF 5 million Pre-Series A financing round. The round will support the industrialization and market introduction of Sonexos’ novel plasma-based technology for active noise control.

Stuttgart / Leinfelden – Bosch is expanding its range of measuring tools and presents a new generation of 18V rotary lasers with the PRO GRL18V-3-31G and PRO GRL18V-4-34CVG. Both tools set new standards, are designed for tough everyday use on construction sites and were developed in close collaboration with users to meet their demanding needs. Thanks to innovative technology and robust design, both tools offer maximum precision, simple and innovative operation, and high reliability. They are perfectly tailored to the needs of tradespeople and professionals who do not want to compromise. Both rotary lasers are part of Bosch's Professional 18V System , which covers all relevant applications with 18V and, thanks to the multi-brand AmpShare alliance , even extends beyond Bosch's offerings. Many brands, many tools, one battery system: All tools can run on the same 18V lithium-ion battery and charger, thus saving tradespeople time, space, and money.

Milan, Italy – The more connected a motorcycle is, the more important it is to protect it against digital attacks. Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, and cloud connections are rapidly gaining importance in the two-wheeler segment. With this in mind, and with a view to protecting vehicle electronics even more effectively, Bosch is unveiling a new, highly compact generation of its Central Gateway at EICMA 2026.

减：直接支付发行费用 1,234.91 二、募集资金净额 278,965.09 减： 以前年度已使用金额 166,114.59 本年度使用金额 11,818.57 暂时补流金额 - 现金管理金额 81,000.00 银行手续费支出及汇兑损益 9.66 加： 募集资金利息收入 736.85 三、报告期期末募集资金余额 20,759.12 二、募集资金管理情况 根据有关法律法规及公司章程的规定，遵循规范、安全、高效、透明的原则，公司制定了《芜湖伯特利汽车安全系统股份有限公司募集资金管理办法》，对募集资金的存储、审批、使用、管理与监督做出了明确的规定，以在制度上保证募集资金的规范使用。 1、2021 年 7 月发行可转债募集资金情况 2021 年 7 月 16 日，本公司与交通银行股份有限公司芜湖分行、中国农业银行股 份有限公司芜湖分行、兴业银行股份有限公司芜湖分行、中国光大银行股份有限公司合肥分行、芜湖扬子农村商业银行股份有限公司公园大道支行及保荐机构国泰君安证券股份有限公司（以下简称国泰君安）分别签订《募集资金专户存储三方监管协议》。 2021 年 8 月 25 日，本公司与 WBTL DE SALTILLO S. de R.L.de C.V.（以下简称 伯特利墨西哥）、芜湖伯特利材料科技有限公司、芜湖伯特利电子控制系统有限公司以及交通银行股份有限公司、中国银行股份有限公司芜湖分行、上海浦东发展银行股份有限公司芜湖分行及保荐机构国泰君安分别签订《募集资金专户存储四方监管协议》。 2022 年 7 月 7 日，本公司与伯特利墨西哥、BANCOBASES.A.I.B.M、保荐机构 国泰君安分别签订《募集资金专户存储四方监管协议》。 2022 年 8 月 23 日，本公司与安徽迪亚拉汽车部件有限公司、中国农业银行股份 有限公司芜湖金桥支行、保荐机构国泰君安分别签订《募集资金专户存储四方监管协议》。 2024 年 1 月 12 日，本公司与威海伯特利汽车安全系统有限公司（以下简称“威海 伯特利”）、中国工商银行股份有限公司乳山支行、保荐机构国泰君安分别签订 《募集 资金专户存储四方监管协议》。 2024 年度，本公司因聘请中国国际金融股份有限公司（以下简称“中金公司”）作 为向不特定对象发行可转换公司债券的保荐机构，并承接原保荐机构国泰君安尚未完 成的持续督导工作。本公司与原保荐机构国泰君安以及相关募集资金存储银行签订的 《募集资金三方监管协议》、《募集资金四方监管协议》相应终止。鉴于本公司保荐机 构的更换，并为进一步规范公司募集资金管理，保护投资者权益，本公司及保荐机构 中金公司与存放募集资金的商业银行重新签署了《募集资金专户存储三方监管协议》 及《募集资金专户存储四方监管协议》。 上述监管协议与上海证券交易所监管协议范本不存在重大差异，监管协议的履行 不存在问题。 募集资金存储情况表 单位：万元 币种：人民币 发行名称 2021 年公开发行可转换公司债券 募集资金到账时间 2021 年 7 月 5 日 账户名称

株式会社アドヴィックス（本社：愛知県刈谷市、社長：秋山晃、以下、アドヴィックス）が新開発したブレーキパッドの「サステナ（新環境規制対応）パッド」が、2026年5月に国内発売されたMAZDA「CX-5」に採用されたことをお知らせします。

【開発背景】 欧州連合が定める自動車の新環境規制「Euro 7」（以下、Euro 7）では、ブレーキ粉塵も規制対象となります。当社が主力とするノンアスベスト（NAO）材は環境負荷が低い一方で、欧州で主流のロースチール材と比較し制動力の面で課題がありました。アドヴィックスは、規制値のクリアと高い制動力の両立を目指して進めてきました。

【製品概要】 本製品は、材料に石綿や銅を含まないNAO材をベースに耐熱性に優れた有機材や無機材、セラミックなどの配分を高め、環境規制値※1を満たしながら高い制動力を実現させた点が特長です。開発にはAI活用による配合パターンのシミュレーションなども活用し、多くの試験評価を経て本製品の優位性が認められ、製品化にいたりました。

アドヴィックスは今後も、電動化や環境規制などで発生する課題に対し、顧客視点で迅速なソリューションを提供し続けてまいります。

株式会社アドヴィックス（本社：愛知県刈谷市、社長：秋山晃、以下、アドヴィックス）は、愛知県が推進する女性活躍促進施策において、2026年6月10日に「あいち女性の活躍プロモーションリーダー」に認定されました。

「あいち女性の活躍プロモーションリーダー」は、愛知県が、県全体の女性活躍を県と共に推進する企業に交付されます。「あいち女性の活躍プロモーションリーダー」に認定されるには、「あいち女性輝きカンパニー」の認証を取得している必要があり、アドヴィックスは、2024年7月に認証を取得しています。

当社の女性活躍やダイバーシティ推進の最大の特徴は、女性従業員が主体となり、誰もが働きやすくなるための施策を考え、経営に提案し、実現していることにあります。例えば、女性同士がキャリア形成や育児との両立について気軽に相談・交流できる女性交流サロンや、先輩ママの声を盛り込んだ復職ガイドの作成、製造現場では女性ならではの視点を活かした高さや重さに関する作業環境の改善やマタニティウエアの導入など、当事者の声を大切にしながら働きやすい職場づくりを進めています。また、両立支援の取り組みなども評価され、2025年12月に「プラチナくるみん」認定を取得しています。

アドヴィックスは今後、「あいち女性の活躍プロモーションリーダー」として、女性活躍に関する取り組みや知見の発信・共有を通じて、地域全体の取り組みに寄与していきます。

アドヴィックスは、電動化や自動運転に対応する製品ラインアップの拡充とソフトウェアで様々な価値を提案し、新たなモビリティ社会の実現に貢献してまいります。

株式会社アドヴィックス（本社：愛知県刈谷市、社長：秋山晃、以下、アドヴィックス）は、ドイツ自動車工業会（VDA）が設計した情報セキュリティの基準であるTISAX（Trusted Information Security Assessment Exchange）認証を取得しました。

近年、自動車業界においては重要な情報を他社と共有し製品を共同開発する動きが活発になっています。共有する情報の中には機密性の高い内容が含まれているため、サプライチェーン全体でセキュリティレベルの把握と高度な情報セキュリティ対策の強化が喫緊で求められています。

TISAXは、自動車業界のサプライチェーン全体で、情報セキュリティ水準を共通の基準で評価・共有するための業界標準の認証（評価）制度です。TISAX認証を取得することで、情報セキュリティレベルを客観的に証明できるため、顧客や取引先からの信頼性が向上します。また、共有プラットフォーム上で評価結果を確認することができるので、個社毎に審査や回答を行う必要がなくなり、取引開始までのプロセスを大幅に効率化できます。今回の本社拠点での認証取得を皮切りに、欧州をはじめとした各地域の開発拠点での取得を目指します。

アドヴィックスは、情報セキュリティ体制の継続的な強化に取り組み、お客様と社会から信頼される企業であり続けてまいります。

BETHESDA, Md . — January 14, 2026 — The Auto Care Association today thanked the United States House Committee on Energy and Commerce’s Subcommittee on Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade (CMT) for holding a timely and important hearing to examine legislative options to strengthen motor vehicle safety, ensure consumer choice and affordability, and cement U.S. automotive leadership.

The association commended Chairman Bilirakis, R-Fla.-12, Ranking Member Schakowsky, D-Ill.-9, and members of the Subcommittee for their leadership and thoughtful consideration of bipartisan solutions that recognize the rapidly evolving nature of vehicle technology and its impact on safety, repair, and consumer costs.

In testimony provided to the subcommittee, Auto Care Association President and CEO Bill Hanvey emphasized that safe, affordable, and accessible vehicle repair is essential to highway safety and consumer protection, particularly as vehicles become increasingly software-driven and data-dependent.

“Today’s vehicles are computers on wheels,” Hanvey said, noting that manufacturers are increasingly restricting access to critical repair and maintenance data. “When vehicle owners and independent repairers are locked out of that data, repairs are delayed, costs increase, and safety can be compromised.”

Hanvey underscored the importance of including the Right to Equitable and Professional Auto Industry Repair (REPAIR) Act (H.R. 1566) in the safety title of the upcoming Surface Transportation Reauthorization Act. He highlighted that the bipartisan legislation, supported by 42 cosponsors and more than 83% of American voters, would immediately enhance safety by ensuring vehicle owners can choose where and how their vehicles are professionally repaired.

Key points from Hanvey’s testimony included:

Cost and safety impacts on consumers : Manufacturer-imposed data restrictions are forcing vehicle owners into franchised dealerships, where repair costs are, on average, 36% higher and wait times significantly longer.

Real-world safety consequences : Independent repair shops are routinely unable to complete even basic repairs—such as battery replacements or windshield wiper changes—without dealer-only codes, resulting in unnecessary delays and added risk for drivers.

Economic and workforce implications : Independent repair shops perform more than 70% of out-of-warranty repairs nationwide and are critical to local economies, workforce development, and vehicle uptime for working families and commercial fleets.

Cybersecurity and intellectual property protections: The REPAIR Act preserves existing intellectual property rights and cybersecurity standards  manufacturers use to deliver data to franchised dealers.

Commercial vehicle safety: With only about 5,600 medium- and heavy-duty truck dealerships nationwide, independent and mobile repair providers are essential to keeping commercial fleets operating safely, especially in rural and remote regions.

Hanvey warned that without federal action, the automotive aftermarket faces an existential threat that would lead to a vertically integrated industry, reduced competition, higher prices, diminished quality, and fewer choices for consumers.

“The REPAIR Act is pro-consumer, pro-safety, and pro-competition,” Hanvey said. “It simply ensures that vehicle owners can access the repair and maintenance data necessary to keep their vehicles safe and on the road—just as they always have.”

Learn more about the REPAIR Act and send a letter to Congress today at repairact.com.

BETHESDA, Md. – Sept. 10, 2025 – Great Place To Work® and Fortune magazine selected the Auto Care Association for the 2025 Fortune Best Workplaces in Consulting and Professional Services™ List. Earning a spot at 35 on this list recognizes the Auto Care Association as one of the best companies to work for in the country. This is the fourth recognition the Auto Care Association has earned for great workplaces and comes in addition to earning the certification of “Great Place to Work” both in 2024 and again in 2025 as well as 2025 Best Small Workplace.

The Best Workplaces in Consulting and Professional Services award is based on an analysis of survey responses from nearly 149,000 employees at Great Place To Work Certified™ companies in the consulting and professional services industry.

“This recognition is a direct reflection of our incredible team,” said Bill Hanvey, president and CEO, Auto Care Association. “Their passion and commitment make this such a special place to work. We’re proud to celebrate them and thankful for everything they do to make honors like this possible.”

The Best Workplaces in Consulting and Professional Services list is highly competitive. Great Place To Work, the global authority on workplace culture, determines its lists using its proprietary Trust Index™ Survey to evaluate and certify thousands of organizations in America’s largest ongoing annual workforce study, based on more than 1.3 million survey responses and data from companies representing more than 8.4 million employees.

“We’re incredibly proud to once again be recognized as a Great Place to Work, now with the additional honor of being named among the best in consulting and professional services,” said Lea Diamond, senior vice president, people operations, Auto Care Association. “These achievements reflect the culture of trust, collaboration, respect—and most importantly, fun—that our employees build every day. Earning back-to-back certifications and this new recognition reinforces our commitment to creating an environment where people feel valued, supported, and inspired to grow.”

Survey responses reflect a comprehensive picture of the workplace experience. Honorees were selected based on their ability to offer positive outcomes for employees regardless of job role, race, gender, sexual orientation, work status or other demographic identifier.

To learn more about working at Auto Care Association, view the association’s Great Place To Work profile or visit https://www.autocare.org/about-us/working-at-auto-care .

Its proprietary platform and Great Place To Work Model help companies evaluate the experience of every employee, with exemplary workplaces becoming Great Place To Work Certified and receiving recognition on a coveted Best Workplaces™ List.

9月11日， 银企行合作赋能汽摩配企业抱团出海暨共建上海国际汽配永久展馆战略发展大会 在上海国际汽车城瑞立酒店召开。本次大会是银、行、企三方协同的一次集中呈现—— 银行赋能给金融支持，行业商会做纽带，企业作为主体积极参与 。三方各尽其责、各展所长，上海国际汽配永久展馆的生态协同效应与平台优势进一步显现。展馆聚微成炬，让分散在产业基地乡镇里的中小汽摩配企业抱团出海，这束火炬，正成为指引中小企业走向全球市场的方向。

全国政协委员、全国工商联汽摩配商会常务会长杨英 在致辞中指出，当前中小企业单独出海成本高、渠道窄、风险大。永久展馆探索的 “基 地制造 、上海展贸、销往全球” 新模式，是商会服务全国会员企业的重要抓手。“永久展馆就是全国汽摩配行业抱团出海的事业起点。”她结合自身在印尼、越南建厂的经历坦言，单打独斗确实非常无奈，呼吁中小企业抱团出海。

上海市政协委员、上海新兴产业投资促进会执行会长、上海致盛实业集团董事长张润斌 表示，上海是我国对外开放的前沿窗口，嘉定更是中国汽车产业的高地。他坦言，中小制造业主体仍面临信息不对称、融资渠道窄、抗风险能力弱等难题，单靠企业单兵作战走不快、走不远。 上海新兴产业促进会将联动金融投资机构、产业园区和 各行业商 协会，主动参与永久展馆的资源对接与产业协同。

上海国际汽车城集团党委委员、副总经理陈杰 ，把汽 车城 25 年产业积 淀与永久展馆的落地逻辑讲得很透。 “无论是一个区域的发展，还是零部件企业发展，都离不开金融和资金的支持。 ” 如今汽车城已集聚上汽大众整车基地，以及理想、蔚来、舍弗勒等企业的研发中心。 他说， 永久展馆落在汽车城，看中的正是“客户就在身边”的产业生态——“好项目不缺空间，好项目不缺资源。 ”

全国工商联汽摩配商会会长、瑞立集团董事长张晓平 发表主旨演讲。 他给出硬核数据：据浙江省汽摩配行业商会统计，浙江全省中小汽摩配企业超过2.6万家，今年全省汽车及零部件产值有望突破1.4万亿元，大部分来自中小企业的配件出口和后市场。“浙江汽配产业的活力和潜力在哪里？在零部件，在中小企业，在出海。”

张晓平指出，中国整车出口今年有望突破 1000 万辆，未来中国汽配出口和海外配套市场将是超万亿级新蓝海。“ 不出海就出局。出海 是加法，不 是减法，企业的总部、税收、产能根基在国内。 ”他强调，中小汽摩配企业单打独斗的时代已经过去，“一个外商到温州、台州汽配制造基地，一天看 4 家企业，待十天也只能看 40 家。 在永久展馆，一天可以看一两千家企业。跑一家胜过跑百家千家。 ”

中国建设银行总行公司业务部资深副经理董宣忠 代表金融机构发声。他表示，建设银行推出“善建智造”“善建科技”两大专项方案，为汽摩配企业智能化改造、产能扩容、品牌出海提供全链条金融赋能。“ 金融正在加快转向服务实体经济。企业在抱团出海的同时，金融也在探讨如何走向全球，我们的目标是一致的。 ”

当天到场的银行阵容强大：建行总行及浙江、上海、广东、江苏、安徽、苏州等分行，农行温州分行、金华分行、丽水分行，民生银行温州分行，工行、邮储、浦发、温州银行瑞安支行等数十家金融机构负责人出席。一张覆盖跨境结算、贸易融资、风险规避的金融服务网络正在永久展馆周边织密。

银行给金融支持，商会做纽带、做服务，企业做主体、做产品——各出一块拼图，拼出的正是永久展馆这个“抱团出海”的产业生态。

永久展馆不仅是物理空间，更是链接全产业链的超级枢纽。当天，来自成都、青岛、山西、宿迁、廊坊、丽水、衢州、达州、南通、贵阳等全国各地的公交集团负责人近百人齐聚永久展馆，带着合作需求而来。通过“国企实力 + 民企活力，成就新质生产力”的协同发展模式， 新瑞立 已与全国 25 个省 110 家公交公司达成合作，公交系统的终端场景将与汽配供应链在永久展馆深度打通。

大会现场，永久展馆分别与河北再制造协会、 GL 出海联盟 达成战略合作，共同打造再制造汽车零部件展厅、GL出海联盟展厅。

从再制造零部件到出海联盟，从跨境电商到法律咨询、仲裁机构，永久展馆正在构建“保姆式”服务闭环，真正实现“进永久展馆，做全球生意”。

大会期间，滁州市委书记吴劲、副市长后其洁一行到访永久展馆参观交流，明确表示要加快推进滁州城市产业会客厅的打造，加快推进滁州公交公司与新瑞立的合作。这是永久展馆城市会客厅版图持续扩容的又一进展。

新瑞立 COO 徐本光发布年度发展报告：新瑞立在全国布局 265 家门店，拥有 30 多万个 SKU 和 1500 家战略供应商，合作客户超过 22 万，产品出口覆盖 100多 个国家和地区。

永久展馆组委会执行主任朱仲升介绍，展馆总建筑面积 5.3 万平方米，规划入驻 3000 家企业，目前入驻已超 2000 家，已建成 21 个城市会客厅。 12 月 1 日，永久展馆将正式全面开馆，届时全国汽摩配商会年会同期举行， 12 月 2 日 法兰克福展 在上海开幕，三大盛会能量叠加。 开馆前将冲刺 3000 家企业入驻，打造 100 个城市会客厅。

大会期间，巴西国际采购团一行 20 余人到访永久展馆，重点筛选中国质优价平的汽车零部件源头工厂，同时考察工程机械零部件供应链资源。 采购团对展馆“ 3000 余家源头制造企业、 365 天常态化运营”的模式高度认可。本次来访，搭建了中巴汽车后市场产业链合作桥梁，助力中国汽配企业开拓广阔的巴西市场。

组委会副主任、首席跨境电商专家李智荣拆解“一链一网一平台”数字化体系，为入驻企业实现全年 365 天、 24 小时不间断全球获客。新瑞立采购总监金丽敏发布国内国际双市场采购需求，将优先对接永久展馆已入驻企业。

答谢晚宴上，瑞安市惠华汽车机油泵有限公司董事长钱继续的一番话，道出了无数中小汽配企业主的心声。

“我们做机油泵的，产品藏在发动机最里面，车开了 20 万公里车主都看不到；我们的厂藏在小镇上，默默无闻。”钱继续动情地说，“我们这一行，一年要跑 50 多个展会，累得半死，但展会一结束，灯一关，人就散了。我们最缺的，不是手艺，是被看见。”

他把展馆广告贴在自己车上，跑遍杭州、宁波、广州。“ 以前是我去找客户，三天展会一散场，回去也没几个。现在是展馆让客户找得到我。 ”他说，一年 2 万元投入，换来的是 365 天的展示和全球流量对接，“这笔账，每一个务实的企业家都算得清楚。”

“相信才能看到，不是看到了才相信。”钱继续说，“我不是站在门口等客户，我是在屋里点一盏灯。今天这盏灯就是上海国际汽配永久展馆，灯已经点亮了， 365 天不灭。”

大会期间，钱继续又追加了一个展位。从“试试看”到“再加一个”，这位做机油泵的企业主，用最实在的方式投出了自己的信任票。

像钱继续这样的中小企业，正是中国汽配产业最真实的底色。浙江 2.6 万家中小汽摩配企业，九成藏在乡镇里，有手艺、有产品，却缺少被世界看见的窗口。让中小企业被看见——这是上海国际汽配永久展馆的初心。 当 2000 多家这样的企业聚在一起，微光便开始汇聚成星海。

但“被看见”只是第一步。 中国汽配品牌向上，正在经历从“被看见”到“被相信”的关键一跃。 永久展馆要做的，正是帮助中小企业在被看见的基础上，用 365 天不间断的展示、稳定的品质、银企护航的信用背书，一步步赢得全球采购商的信任。

截至本次大会，上海国际汽配永久展馆已吸引超过 2000 家企业入驻。 从 2000 家到 3000 家，从 21 个城市会客厅到 100 个，永久展馆的版图还在加速扩大。

银、行、企各尽其责，公交、保险、展会企业等生态伙伴协同共建，聚微成炬，众行致远。这束火炬，正照亮中国汽配产业从“单打独斗”走向“抱团共赢”、从“被看见”走向“被相信”的征途。

以及建行总行、浙江省分行、上海市分行、广东省分行、江苏省分行、安徽省分行、苏州分行，农行温州分行、金华分行、丽水分行，建行温州分行、嘉定支行、马鞍山分行、常州分行、泰州分行、嘉兴分行、湖州分行、台州分行、绍兴分行、丽水分行、舟山分行，农行瑞安支行，民生银行温州分行，工行瑞安支行，邮储瑞安支行，浦发瑞安支行，温州银行瑞安支行，中信银行嘉兴平湖支行、海盐支行，招商银行虹口支行等银行领导。

以及广州公交、重庆公交、天津公交、上海久事公交、四川省公交协会、台州公交、湖州公交、绍兴公交、内江公交、南充公交、包头公交、扬州公交、银川公交、汉中汉运、邯郸公交、灵璧公交、滁州公交、宣城汽运、株洲公交、怀化汽运、巴东公交、阳新公交、菏泽公交、德州公交、洛阳交运、濮阳交运、聊城交运、新郑公交、金山巴士、奉贤巴士、锦山客运、奉贤客运、松江公交、青浦巴士、青浦众兴、太阳岛公交、青浦京申、嘉定公交、露虹公交等公交企业负责人。

以及贵州遵义国家经济技术开发区、贵州遵义汇川区、贵州习水县、重庆璧山区、重庆市大足区、广西柳州柳南、安徽黄山市南陵、江苏泗洪、江苏徐州铜山区、湖北武汉汉阳等地方政府有关部门领导。

8月28日，政行企联动·走进上海永久展馆·赋能汽摩配企业内外贸一体化发展大会在上海国际汽车城瑞立酒店举行。本次大会由全国工商联汽摩配商会、上海国际汽车城集团、长三角汽车后市场产销合作产业链联盟联合主办，瑞立集团·新瑞立汽配连锁承办。

全国多地驻沪办、工信（经信）系统领导为主，工商联、商务、招商、开发区等政府有关单位负责人、各地商协会共同参会； 共商、共建上海国际汽配永久展馆100个城市会客厅。

从1月瑞安首站启航到8月入驻企业突破1700家，上海国际汽配永久展馆正加速成型。大会期间，永久展馆正式官宣： 银企战略合作千人大会定于9月11日在上海国际汽车城瑞立酒店举行。多位与会嘉宾表示，随着入驻企业持续增加，展馆核心铺位资源日趋紧张，9月11日千人大会后很可能出现一铺难求的局面。政行企三方正式从“走进”迈向“共建”。

上海市嘉定区人民政府副区长丁炯炯 在致辞中表示，上海国际汽配永久展馆作为赋能产业的重要载体， 已吸引1700家企业入驻。 展馆集常态展示、精准对接、专业招商、综合服务于一体，充分发挥嘉定汽车产业集聚和资源链接优势。 嘉定将持续优化营商环境，完善产业支持政策，为企业提供全周期、全方位的支持， 助力打通国内国际市场渠道，实现内外贸协同发展。

中国民营经济研究会常务理事、浙江省政府特约研究员、浙商研究中心副主任蔡晓春 在致辞中，一针见血地指出了大会主题的关键转变： “走进”是被动的参观、临时的使用；“共建”是主动的参与、长期的投入。

他指出，当前汽摩配产业面临整零协同不充分、出海体系化能力不足、跨界转型存在技术鸿沟三大痛点，解决这些问题需要“有为政府+有效市场+友好生态”三方协同。 共建永久展馆意味着三个转变：政府从管理者转变为赋能者，商协会从联谊会转变为资源整合平台，展馆从交易场转变为价值共创平台。新瑞立+永久展馆是双轮驱动，本质是产业互联网与实体展贸的深度融合。 只有三方联动，才能让中小企业“出海有保障、回来有港湾”。

湖北省人民政府驻上海办事处主任周彬 ，用湖北汽摩配企业抱团入驻永久展馆的实践，分享了驻沪办赋能地方产业内外贸一体化发展的经验。湖北正打造“ 武孝襄随十 ”万亿级汽车产业新格局， 依托永久展馆已落地十堰、襄阳两大会客厅，近百家鄂企入驻运营。 展馆对地方企业形成三重赋能：帮助立足上海、辐射全球，擦亮区域品牌；精准对接长三角主机厂与海内外贸易商；搭建商务洽谈平台助力内外贸融合发展。

全国工商联汽摩配商会会长、瑞立集团董事长张晓平 在主旨发言中指出，国内汽车市场已高度内卷，未来五到十年将迎来深度洗牌。而海外万亿级蓝海正加速打开，今年中国整车出口有望突破1000万台。 结论只有六个字：不出海，就出局。

针对部分地方政府担心企业“走出去”会导致产业空心化，张晓平算了一笔账： 出海不是减法而是加法，是“在国内做存量、在海外做增量”。 企业发展好了，总部、税收、产能的根还在当地。把企业搭载在永久展馆平 台上等于给企业 装上翅膀 ， 企业的市场越能海阔天空，企业的根就能扎得越稳，对当地“栽好梧桐树、养好金凤凰”就越有利。

上海国际汽车城集团党委委员、副总经理陈杰 介绍，作为全国汽车产业集聚度最高的区域之一，汽车城已汇聚上汽大众、蔚来、理想、博世等头部企业，每年举办200余场产业会议，持续凝聚行业核心力量。 依托高度集中的产业资源，永久展馆打造了一站式高效对接平台，外商单日即可触达上千家企业，效率远超传统考察模式。 放眼全球，汽车城正谋划公共出海平台，为企业拓展国际市场赋能，推动产业链抱团出海，形成全球化竞争合力。

上海国际汽配永久展馆组委会执行主任朱仲升 汇报最新数据： 展馆入驻企业已超1700家，11月底冲刺3000家。 总建筑面积 5.3万平 方米，已建成20个城市产业会客厅。传统展会三五天热闹，永久展馆365天细水长流， 200多批国内外商贸代表团，体现了蓬勃的产业能量。

上海国际汽配永久展馆组委会副主任、首席跨境电商专家李智荣 详解“一链一网一平台”线上线下闭环：3000家供应链为“一链”，全域流量网为“一网”，产业互联网平台为“一平台”， 七个维度流量来源实现全年不间断全球获客 。

新瑞立采购总监金丽敏 发布百亿采购计划： 去年采购超30亿元，未来5年将冲向每年百亿的采购额， 其 中出口50亿元，将优先对接入驻企业。 平台对外全面开放，入驻企业品牌将通过海外20多场专业展会持续曝光。

大会现场， 张晓平分别与国家外贸转型升级基地（上海嘉定·汽车及零部件）副总经理徐明、 星鼎荟中国汽车后市场企业家俱乐部 洪耿戈签署战略合作协 议。 这标志着永久展馆的“共建”朋友圈再扩容——嘉定基地带 来政策与口 岸资源，广东星鼎荟注入渠道与市场活力 ， 长三角和大湾区加强联动， 内外贸一体化发展再提速。

奖项背后，是公司在高端制造领域近三十年的深厚积淀。瑞立科密已入选 国家级专精特新 “小巨人”企业、国家级制造业单项冠军 ，近七年 两次荣获国家科学技术进步二等奖 。

这意味着，瑞立科密所擅长的，正是机器人从实验室走向量产所亟需的 “工业化能力”——这也是当前人形机器人产业最稀缺的环节之一。

在圆桌对话中，瑞立科密总经理 黄万义 指出： “人形机器人当前面临的最大挑战，并非技术原理的创新，而是 从样机到万台级量产过程中的成本控制、一致性与供应链韧性 。这正是瑞立科密在汽车工业中锤炼数十年的核心能力——我们有信心将这一 ' 基本功 ' 转化为机器人赛道的竞争优势。”

面对具身智能产业加速落地的窗口期，瑞立科密积极关注机器人赛道的投资布局，依托自身制造能力与技术积累，探索通过战略投资、产业合作等方式切入机器人核心零部件领域，稳步拓展第二增长曲线。

面向未来，瑞立科密将坚持技术创新，立足制造根基，以长期积累赋能机器人产业高质量发展，与全球伙伴共创具身智能新未来。

Ask most people how a damper is tuned and they will picture an engineer at a test track, adjusting something until the car feels right. That moment is real, and it is still where sign-off happens. But by the time the car turns a wheel, most of the decisions have already been made. Marcin Knapczyk, Chief Engineer at BWI Group, explains the process of damper tuning.

A long way from the car. It all starts with the customer and what they want to achieve. We normally work to a statement of requirements the size of a small book. It defines what the product needs to do and therefore what needs to be tested: durability requirements, hot and cold temperature ranges, all the different conditions the vehicle will meet in its life. Alongside that sits the performance target.

So the requirements are set. How does the system get into the vehicle?

Every project starts with integrating the system into the customer’s architecture. For semi-active system like MagneRide, that means aligning our software with their control environment and making sure everything communicates properly. Only once the system is operational do we begin calibration, adjusting control parameters to match the ride and handling characteristics the customer is after.

We have become more modular about how that works. We can supply a complete MagneRide system, including the dampers, sensors, ECUs and software, or just the individual components required. Some customers want full system delivery and tuning support. Others prefer to embed our control algorithms into their own ECUs.

Once you are up and running, what are you actually looking for?

We refine the system through real-world testing, evaluating ride comfort, body control, noise and vibration levels and overall vehicle dynamics, and we work towards whatever the customer wants the car to be, whether that is sharp handling for a performance model or a more composed ride in an electric SUV.

Underneath those targets are two things we have to control at once. Primary ride is body movement. Secondary ride is wheel control. MagneRide can respond in just a few milliseconds, which allows us to control both precisely. On a challenging surface such as an uneven country road, that responsiveness makes a real difference: we can maintain strong body control without introducing harshness from the wheels. Other systems often reach a point where they have to increase damping to control the body, and that leads to an overly stiff ride.

When the driver comes back with feedback, how quickly can you act on it?

That is what magnetorheological damping changed. Traditional passive systems use valves, which often require physical hardware changes during development. You are manufacturing and swapping out multiple sets of valves to refine the tuning, and that is time-consuming and resource-intensive. Ride Van, our mobile laboratory, travels and resides at a customer’s site (proving ground) where physical changes are made

With MagneRide we do not need to change any hardware during tuning. The damping force is controlled digitally through software, so our ride engineers can make changes directly from a laptop. That gives us much more agility in development, reduces cost and speeds up the entire calibration process.

How much of the final judgement is still subjective?

Subjective evaluation is a critical part of sign-off, and it is not going away. The complexity of modern vehicles, with all the subsystems in a modern chassis, makes it extremely difficult to do everything virtually, and an expert driver can evaluate the car across many conditions in a very short time. In subjective evaluation your body is the sensor, and you cannot simulate that. Even with all the AI we have now, it is difficult to describe what we are looking for.

How do you know when a tune is finished?

The bench test verifies durability and, in a more limited way, performance. The vehicle is where we verify that performance and define the nominal damper that is then reproduced in series production. After the ride session we have a master set, which is the evidence of what the customer tested.

How is simulation changing the shape of all this?

One of the biggest impacts is the reduction in the number of physical prototypes. One OEM told us they can now build ten times fewer test vehicles for a new vehicle generation than before, and a prototype car is extraordinarily expensive. The downside is that there is less access to prototype vehicles, which in turn encourages more virtual testing. It follows through to us as well: fewer prototype vehicles mean fewer prototype dampers to produce. Where simulation helps us most is FEA and CFD, predicting failures and avoiding them, which reduces the number of samples required.

So where does damper development go next?

It will continue to move towards bench testing. Using hardware in the loop to extend virtual testing and validate your models is much more cost effective and quicker than track testing, and you want the product to be as mature as possible before progressing to in-vehicle testing. But there will always be a need for physical vehicle dynamics testing.

The other direction is software. As EV adoption increases, expectations around noise and ride quality rise with it. Without engine noise to mask imperfections, every bump and vibration becomes more noticeable, and the added mass of an EV makes controlling body motion more challenging. At the same time the shift towards software-defined vehicles is accelerating the need for digitally controlled suspension that can be integrated and updated easily.

Battery electric vehicles accounted for 20% of new EU car registrations in the first five months of 2026, up from 15.3% a year earlier, according to ACEA . Add hybrids and plug-in hybrids and more than two thirds of new cars are electrified.

OEMs have a decision to make with electrified vehicles. Use regenerative braking; blending regen with the friction brakes as necessary. Or solely rely on lift-off regen, which is how one-pedal driving became a defining EV behaviour. The first maximises range but typically has poor brake pedal feel, the other has an unaffected brake pedal but is wasting energy.

The handover is where the driver feels the friction brakes take over from regen part-way through a stop. This is particularly noticeable in the last 10km/h of a stop because the electric motor needs to be rotating to generate torque. There are a multitude of variations that mean making brake pedal feel consistent is a real challenge. For example, when the battery is in a high state of charge full regen is unavailable, so the same pedal input produces a different response compared to when the battery is low. Battery temperature, brake temperatures, brake pedal force  – these all impact what blend of regen and friction brake is required.

An integrated electronic brake system, such as our iDBC 1-Box, decouples the brake pedal from the brakes themselves. A travel sensor and a pressure sensor read driver intention, an ECU decides how the demand is met, and a motor-driven pressure supply unit builds hydraulic pressure at the wheels. The pedal simply becomes an input signal where the force-travel characteristic/ resistance , or the feel, can be tuned through software.

Through this approach pedal feel can be calibrated to the character of the vehicle: firm and short for a performance derivative, progressive and light for a luxury saloon, and switchable between drive modes on the same car. Decoupling the brake provides better control of the deceleration whether the stop is served by regen, friction or a blend, and regardless of battery state of charge.

An added benefit of an integrated electronic system is that the motor builds pressure around three times faster than a vacuum booster. Reaching full pressure sooner in an autonomous emergency braking situation at highway speeds has a significant impact on stopping distances.

In urban conditions, the energy consumed during braking of pure electric vehicles generally accounts for about 30% of the total energy consumption of vehicle operatio n. So optimising regenerative braking can have a significant impact on a vehicle’s usable range. The limiting factor is often how confidently the braking system can hold friction out of the blend.

A coupled system has to bring friction brakes in early because the pedal is mechanically linked. A decoupled system can serve the majority of the stop through regen wherever grip, temperature and battery conditions allow, introducing friction only when demand exceeds what the electric machine can absorb. The driver feels one consistent pedal throughout.

What happens if the electronics fail on a decoupled brake pedal? Our iDBC was designed around fail-safe operation from the concept stage. The system is developed to ASIL-D and a direct hydraulic path from the pedal pushrod to the calipers remains as a mechanical backup. Even under a fault condition that disables every electronic system on the vehicle, the driver can still stop the car.

A brake system needs to be proven durable and safe across the full operating envelope, which is why the iDBC has been through high and low temperature programmes and a full winter test cycle on ice and snow at our low-adherence facility in Arjeplog, northern Sweden.

The nuances of subjective driving characteristics, such as pedal feel, steering weight and damper tuning, can be key brand differentiators, but noticed, in truth, mainly by enthusiasts and the engineers who created them.

Brake pedal feel in the EV era is different. Poor blending is not a nuance and it is immediately obvious to all drivers, whether they can name it or not. It erodes confidence in the car, and confidence is harder to rebuild than it is to lose.

The ambition, then, is not necessarily a pedal feel that impresses. It is a pedal the driver never thinks about. That is a higher bar than it sounds and it is easier to achieve when the pedal is decoupled and software controlled.

BWI Group’s Technical Centre Krakow has developed a bespoke artificial intelligence (AI) FEA tool. In a recent demonstration project it cut air spring development time from weeks to roughly one hour and uncovered a viable design that experienced engineers had already ruled out. We sat down with Miroslaw Siemieniuk, FEA Manager at BWI Group, to find out how it works, what it found, and why he believes the engineer’s role becomes more important, not less.

Q: Miroslaw, let’s start with the wider picture. Why have you and the team developed this AI-powered FEA tool?

A: That’s agood question. The automotive industry has changed rapidly over the last 10 years or so. Due to safety and electrification vehicles continue to increase in mass and at the same time development timescales are reducing. This is having a significant impact on chassis engineers, who are now being asked to land on tighter performance targets inside narrower programme windows.

Air suspension is a good example of where these pressures are being felt. Ride, handling, comfort and durability are governed by a large set of design variables that interact in tightly coupled, non-linear ways and resolving them is challenging. So there was a clear opportunity here to benefit from the potential AI has to offer.

Q: Walk us through how an air spring is typically developed today. Where does the bottleneck sit?

A: Typically, the starting point is a force-versus-displacement performance curve supplied by the OEM. This defines exactly what the air spring is required to deliver across its full stroke. Our aim is to try and develop a product that matches that curve as closely as possible.

However, due to the many linked interactions of the various components in an air suspension system, hitting that curve and satisfying a number of other conflicting requirements and constraints is rarely straightforward. Internal geometry, working pressure, sleeve material behaviour and reinforcement layout all influence the result. The current approach is iterative manual design, with each step supported by finite element analysis (FEA). For a capable team, converging on a workable design typically takes several weeks.

Q: How does the new AI-powered FEA tool change that?

A: In short,it replaces the repeated manual iteration with a deep-learning surrogate that evaluates design changes almost instantly. This is why Ai in engineering can excel. On the particular air spring used in this study, the full optimisation completed in approximately one hour. So, compared to a typical two-week baseline, that is a 98 percent reduction in process time.

Q: How is the deep-learning model built?

A: The surrogate is a five-layer deep neural network. Importantly, it has been trained on a set of 180 high-quality FEA datasets. Those datasets came from simulation models that had already been correlated against extensive laboratory testing. So we know the models have been physically verified and the network is learning from solid engineering data.

From that training set, the network learns the mapping between the air spring’s design parameters and its resulting force-displacement behaviour and is then used as a fast-evaluating surrogate for the underlying FEA. As with all simulation processes, accuracy and correlation are critical. Against the simulation reference, the model achieved an R-squared of 0.99. In other words, there is strong agreement between its predictions and full FEA outputs.

Q: What design parameters does the model currently optimise?

A: At present, the neural network is wrapped around five design parameters: piston radius, low support radius, sleeve thickness, design pressure and nylon fibre cord angles. A Newton-based optimisation algorithm drives the search, looking for the combination of those parameters that minimises the residual error between the surrogate’s predicted force-displacement curve and the OEM’s target. The resulting root mean square error came in at approximately two percent, which indicates that the expected system behaviour closely matches the target. Once an optimal configuration is identified, the candidate design is subjected to a final detailed FEA for validation.

Q: Did the model uncover anything that was unexpected?

A: It certainly did. During the manual phase of the project, the team had concluded that the target force-displacement curve could not be matched within the existing architecture without adding a specific structural constraint component.

However, the AI tool had a different answer. It identified a combination of parameters that met the target curve inside the defined parameter space without the additional component. Manual iteration had not highlighted it because the number of interacting variables put it outside what could realistically be searched by hand inside any reasonable programme timeline.

It is important to emphasise that this is a demonstration of feasibility. The project has not been signed off for production. Translating it into hardware would still require full testing and validation. But, I think it clearly demonstrates the value of AI in surfacing non-intuitive solutions.

Automated roll control system can be connected and disconnected on demand while driving at speed

SARC removes the compromise between handling and comfort while also improving off-road capabilities

Its unique hydraulic architecture enables mode transitions at any suspension travel and even under load

BWI Group has developed an automated active roll control system. The latest update to the company’s SARC (Semi Active Roll Control) product features a new ‘automatic mode’ that enables a vehicle’s anti-roll bar to disconnect and reconnect seamlessly on demand while driving at speed.

The update addresses an increasing challenge in modern chassis engineering as vehicle mass continues to grow. With SUVs accounting for more than half of new car registrations in Europe in 2024, and BEVs typically around 30% heavier than equivalent ICE models, engineers are increasingly forced to compromise between roll stiffness for handling and compliance for comfort. Heavier vehicles necessitate stiffer stabiliser bars, which extenuates the issue.

SARC’s automatic mode aims to remove this compromise. By disconnecting the bar during normal driving, the system allows the vehicle to adopt a softer, more compliant baseline, only engaging the stabiliser bar when required. The control unit uses vehicle data, such as steering angle, speed, lateral acceleration and yaw rate, to determine when the bar needs to reconnect. During high-speed cornering, for example, it reconnects in less than 200 milliseconds and is imperceptible to the driver.

“Chassis engineers are continually trying to improve road handling and comfort, but the two goals are often incompatible,” said Bruno Perree, Engineering Manager at BWI Group. “The latest update to SARC removes that compromise, allowing engineers to optimise the roll bar purely for handling as it will be disconnected the majority of the time. This not only improves comfort but also adds significant off-road capability, which can be a key competitive differentiator in a crowded SUV market.”

At the core of the system is a compact rotary actuator paired with a fully self-contained hydraulic mechanism. The hydraulic architecture enables the bar to be connected or disconnected even when the wheels are unevenly articulated, which is something mechanical solutions typically cannot achieve. Automatic self-centring using the company’s EZ-Latch™ technology ensures consistent engagement throughout the suspension travel.

SARC is in production on several global platforms, most recently the GWM Tank series, where it is used to balance on-road composure with off-road traction. The addition of SARC’s automatic mode is expected to broaden its application to a wider range of SUVs and BEVs, where managing mass and maintaining ride quality have become central engineering priorities.
